points.name: apps.media.control.register_other
points.interpretation: The two builder paths register the shared callback for control items in the ordinary branches; the actual item and availability depend on the media view state.

points.name: apps.media.control.register_23
points.interpretation: The two builder paths assign item type 3 or 2, respectively from an iteration over items 2 and 3, and register the common media callback.

points.name: apps.media.control.register_4
points.interpretation: The two builder paths register the common callback in the item-4 branch subject to view and connectivity conditions.

points.name: apps.media.control.event_code
points.interpretation: The shared callback checks for event code 7 before dispatching an operation based on current control metadata.

points.name: apps.media.control.current_target
points.interpretation: The callback reads its current object and uses the first byte of its object-associated metadata to choose the control operation.

evidence: The media builder registers the same callback in multiple branches. The callback fetches the event code and current target, requires code 7 and a non-null target, then reads the type byte of object-associated metadata. Types 0..3 route command values 5, 6, 3 and 2 through the player-control function; types 4 and 5 enter other navigation branches. The page lifecycle publishes and clears the main view state.
scope: Only the listed registration/getter call sites while the media main view state is present. Other command sources, registration calls and media pages are outside scope.
limitations: Do not substitute arbitrary current-target pointers; the callback dereferences target-associated data. Rewriting code or registration can desynchronize UI and remote playback state. The recorder of command values does not establish their complete public semantics across player backends. Shared-entry publication and rollback require system-wide quiescence; device behavior is unverified.
